source_files.role: Ported here. load/store/detectVersion are reproduced; isValid and isSemanticallyValid are not (see gaps).
Ported here. Source of the 1.3.0 schema default, the clear-before-load rule, the extension check on store and the whole detectVersion algorithm.
Ported here. The write path plus the three public analysisXML value types (IdentificationHit, SpectrumIdentification, Identification); its stream read path is dead code and is not ported.

Ported here. writeTo and its helpers (writeMetaInfos_, writeEnzyme_, writeModParam_, writeFragmentAnnotations_, trimOpenMSfileURI, writePeptideHit and writeXLMSPeptideHit) are the ordinary and cross-linking writer paths this module reproduces.

Not ported as a header, but it is the read path MzIdentMLFile::load actually uses, so its behaviour is what this module's reader reproduces or deliberately diverges from. Its own ledger entry belongs to a later stage.

Not ported as a header. Read in full: every reference-resolution rule, the score-selection order, the modification-location inference of issue #5443, the cross-linking branches (parseSpectrumIdentificationItemSetXLMS and the XL half of parsePeptideSiblings_) and the reader-side defects recorded in OpenMS_CPP_ISSUES.md come from this file.
The oracle. 15 START_SECTIONs; tests/mzidentml.rs covers both the nine non-cross-linking sections and the six cross-linking sections.

The schema the adapter declares. Read for the element order of SequenceCollection and SpectrumIdentificationProtocol, for which attributes are required (chargeState, experimentalMassToCharge, rank, passThreshold, peptide_ref, dBSequence_ref), for the optional userParam 'type' attribute, and for the Modification location convention (0 = N-terminus, length + 1 = C-terminus) that the writer's C-terminal divergence rests on.

Not ported as a header. Read for the six post-processing functions readMzIdentMLFile calls on a cross-linking document (addProteinPositionMetaValues, addBetaAccessions, addXLTargetDecoyMV, removeBetaPeptideHits, computeDeltaScores, addPercolatorFeatureList); those six are reproduced as private helpers of src/format/mzidentml.rs, because the mzIdentML read path is not meaningful without them. The rest of the header - candidate enumeration, database digestion, spectrum matching, Percolator plumbing - is a search algorithm and keeps its own ledger entry.

Not ported as a header. Implementation of the six post-processing functions above, read at lines 960-1250: the protein-coordinate formula, the beta accession list, the per-chain target/decoy rule, the beta-hit merge and its spectrum grouping, the delta-score ratios and the 32-entry Percolator feature list. The merge keeps only the first hit of every identification. BetaPepEv:start/end numeric appends correctly use StringUtils.h global overloads and are not a character-narrowing defect.
Global numeric string append overloads establish decimal BetaPepEv position formatting.
appendToStr integer implementations use std::to_chars for decimal output.

fixtures.role: Unmodified upstream 1.1.0 document written by OpenMS itself: one run, Mascot 2.1.0, two DBSequences with sequences, four Peptides, six PeptideEvidences with pre/post and isDecoy but no start/end, three SpectrumIdentificationResults covering three different score types (PSM-level q-value, X\!Tandem:hyperscore, Mascot:score), a 0.5 PSM-level statistical threshold, activityDate 2006-01-12T12:13:14, and a SearchModification block whose third entry is Acetyl with a peptide N-term specificity rule. The store, thresholds and regression sections all use it.

Unmodified upstream MS-GF+ export: two SpectrumIdentifications over two SpectrumIdentificationLists, five results, MinCharge/MaxCharge instead of a charges list, missedCleavages=1000, a protein N-terminal Xlink:DTSSP[88] search modification, one Carbamidomethyl Modification at location 19, and PeptideEvidences with 1-based start/end. It also carries two deliberately dangling references - SearchProtocol_99 from the second SpectrumIdentification and SearchDB_99 from DBSeq99 - which is why neither may be an error.

Unmodified upstream regression fixture for issue #5443: five peptides whose Modification elements omit the optional location attribute, covering N-terminal Acetyl (inferred), Oxidation (ambiguous, skipped), Amidated (exclusively C-terminal, inferred), a control with a valid location, and Acetyl with residues="K" (residue-specific, skipped).

Unmodified upstream three-run document: three SpectrumIdentifications over three SpectrumIdentificationLists sharing one SpectrumIdentificationProtocol, three distinct SpectraData locations, and a ppm parent tolerance.

Unmodified upstream 1.3.0 cross-linking document from the mzIdentML crosslinking extension: two SpectrumIdentificationResults, four cross-link items whose MS:1002509/MS:1002510 cvParams carry small integer link values, SearchModifications that repeat those terms, and xiFDR as the analysis software. Exercises the grouping, the 1.3.0 store/load round trip and the spectrum-reference requirement of upstream section 12.

Unmodified upstream 1.2.0 OpenPepXL export of a labelled cross-link search (cross_link:name DSS with a 12.075321 isotope shift): ten SpectrumIdentificationResults whose spectrumID names two spectra, up to four items per result (alpha and beta, each light and heavy), MS:1002511 grouping values, per-item retention times, Fragmentation blocks with cross-link_chain and cross-link_ioncategory arrays, cross_link:mass 138.0680796 and cross_link:mass_isoshift 12.075321. Source of every literal in upstream section 10.

Unmodified upstream 1.2.0 OpenPepXL export of an unlabelled cross-link search: three results, one of them a cross-link pair and two label-free mono-links with no MS:1002511 value at all, an XLMOD:02001 donor modification and two UNIMOD Xlink:DSS[156] mono-linkers. Source of every literal in upstream section 11.

Unmodified upstream 1.3.0 noncovalent-association document: it declares MS:1002494 but no peptide carries a crosslink donor, so it exercises the reader's fallback to the linear item path, with two associated peptides in one result and a ProteinDetectionList.

Unmodified upstream 1.3.0 EDC document: 16 results mixing cross-linked and standalone peptides, 54 MS:1002511 groups with several matches per spectrum, and an Enzyme whose SiteRegexp is a CDATA section - which is why it also pins that CDATA is character data rather than unsupported XML content.

Unmodified upstream 1.3.0 document with three SpectrumIdentificationLists (HCD, ETD, MS3) over six results, so the reader keeps one identification per spectrum reference across several runs. Upstream section 15.

source_anchors.operation: the adapter is constructed with /SCHEMAS/mzIdentML1.3.0.xsd and version 1.3.0, and MzIdentMLHandler::writeTo then hard-codes 1.3.0 again instead of using schema_version_
load clears both output containers before parsing, because the DOM handler only appends; this port returns an owned document and replaces atomically instead
store throws UnableToCreateFile when the filename does not carry the mzid extension, before the handler runs
detectVersion reads the first 15 trimmed lines joined by a space, prefers version="x.y.z" over the mzIdentML/x.y namespace, and falls back to the adapter default
a Xerces parse failure is logged and execution continues; only a null document raises ParseError, so a malformed mzIdentML can be read as a partial document

every element is reached through getElementsByTagName, a document-wide scan that ignores nesting, so elements under the wrong parent are still collected; namespace processing is off, so a document that binds mzIdentML to a prefix matches no tag at all
PeptideEvidence start and end are parsed together, so a failure on either leaves both unknown; both are stored without the 1-based to 0-based conversion OpenMS PeptideEvidence documents
pre and post are taken as text[0] of a possibly empty attribute value, which yields the null character for pre=""
SearchParameters.db is the SearchDatabase location attribute, not the DatabaseName, and a dangling searchDatabase_ref default-constructs an empty DatabaseInput through std::map::operator[]
an absent activityDate becomes DateTime::now(), which makes a load unreproducible; this port leaves the date absent
the run identifier is a fresh UniqueIdGenerator value, with the source's own TODO asking for the XML id; this port uses the SpectrumIdentification element id
missedCleavages below zero, or unreadable, is 'assumed unlimited' and becomes 1000
the protocol writes into pro_id_->at(si_pro_map_[sil_ref]), where a dangling SpectrumIdentificationList reference yields index 0 through std::map::operator[] and silently retargets the first run
the XL-MS branch calls pep_id_->back() immediately after the XL item scan, which is undefined when that scan pushed nothing
a SpectrumIdentificationResult's retention time comes from MS:1000894 or MS:1000016 and is multiplied by 60 when the unit accession is UO:0000031 (minutes)
rank 0 is treated as 1 for PMF data, but an unreadable rank stays 0 and rank - 1 then underflows PeptideHit's unsigned rank

the score scan walks the cvParams in lexicographic accession order (a std::map), takes the first q-value child term while skipping MS:1002055, then any MS:1001143 descendant, then any e-value child term; an item with none of those produces no PeptideHit at all
pep_map_[peptide_ref] default-constructs an empty AASequence for a dangling peptide_ref, so the PSM silently loses its sequence

pass_threshold is stored with setMetaValue(String, bool), which promotes the bool to int because DataValue has no boolean constructor; DataValue::toBool then throws on the value the reader itself wrote
every PeptideEvidence of the referenced Peptide is attached to the PSM, not just the ones its PeptideEvidenceRef children name, because the source calls those references redundant
db_sq_map_[dpv] default-constructs, so a PeptideEvidence pointing at an undeclared DBSequence yields an empty protein accession and inserts a ProteinHit with an empty accession into the run
every ProteinDetectionList is applied to pro_id_->back(), whichever run it belongs to, and each hypothesis is appended without checking for an existing accession
inferModificationLocation_ prefers the N-terminus, assigns the C-terminus only for modifications that are not also internal, and refuses to infer anything when residues names a concrete amino acid
parsePeptideSiblings_ dereferences the first child of PeptideSequence without a null check, so a schema-valid empty <PeptideSequence/> crashes the reader
a SubstitutionModification writes through as[toInt32(location) - 1] with no bounds check, an out-of-bounds heap write driven by a file attribute

findSearchParameters_ maps userParams taxonomy, charges, MinCharge/MaxCharge (which win over charges) and NumTolerableTermini (cast to EnzymaticDigestion::Specificity unchecked) and keeps every other param, including every cvParam, as metadata
the writer's peptide_result_details_ set is built with getAllChildTerms, descendants only, because the parent MS:1001143 has no numeric value
onEndElement accumulates parsed items into current_spectrum_id_, which nothing ever stores, so the handler's documented read mode discards everything it parses

every emitted id (SOF_, SIL_, SIP_, SDAT_, SDB_, PROT_, PEP_, PEV_, SIR_, SII_, ENZ_) is a UniqueIdGenerator value, so two stores of one document differ; the elements are then emitted from std::set<std::string>, i.e. sorted by their own XML text
when both modification lists are empty the writer infers them from the peptides with ModificationDefinitionsSet::inferFromPeptides, adding search parameters the input never declared
an invalid run date becomes DateTime::now() for the activityDate attribute, and line 979 stamps DateTime::now() into the root creationDate
writeMetaInfos_ puts the XSD type of a userParam into unitName instead of the schema's type attribute, so every typed userParam is read back as text

writeModParam_ resolves a modification name with searchModifications and writes one SearchModification per match, so an ambiguous name multiplies; its specificity rules cover the peptide termini only, with a TODO for the protein termini

the C-terminal Modification is written at location = sequence size, while the schema and the source's own reader put the C-terminus at size + 1, so a store/load cycle moves the modification onto the last residue
a PeptideEvidence whose protein accession has no DBSequence is skipped with a log line, dropping the evidence from the output
PeptideEvidence start and end are written as the OpenMS position plus one, which is correct on its own but compounds the reader's missing minus one into a shift per round trip
passThreshold comes from the hit's pass_threshold meta value, else from comparing the score against the run's significance threshold when one was set, else 1

the score cvParam chain is: a score type naming an MS:1001143 descendant, then the same by accession, then q-value/FDR, Posterior Error Probability, OMSSA, Mascot, XTandem, SEQUEST, MS-GF+ and OpenPepXL:score aliases, then the bare parent term plus a userParam carrying the number
the fallback userParam for an unmapped score type is the only place the number survives, and no reader recovers it, so such a score type does not round-trip

writeFragmentAnnotations_ matches annotations against a regex whose charge group is written as a character class, so the charge comes from PeakAnnotation::charge and any annotation that does not fit the mzIdentML fragment structure is skipped
xl_ms_search_ is set by scanning every AdditionalSearchParams for MS:1002494 before anything else is read, and it switches the whole document onto the cross-linking path

the items of one SpectrumIdentificationResult are grouped by the value of their MS:1002511 cvParam, with an index that counts every element child of the result, and an empty grouping falls back to the first item alone
a match is labelled only when the light and heavy experimental m/z differ and the spectrumID names more than one spectrum; the light half is the smallest m/z
a donor position of -1 becomes xl_pos1 0 with N_TERM, one equal to the sequence length becomes length-1 with C_TERM, and anything else keeps its position with ANYWHERE

the XL branch of parsePeptideSiblings_ records donor and acceptor link values and positions, the cross-linker name from the first UNIMOD/XLMOD cvParam and the monoisotopicMassDelta, and registers a peptide whose only cross-linking evidence is an Xlink/XLMOD modification as its own mono-link

removeBetaPeptideHits folds the beta chain's evidences into BetaPepEv: metadata, keeps only the first hit of every identification, and then collects the identifications of one spectrum reference into one identification with the OpenPepXL:score score type
addPercolatorFeatureList sets feature_extractor to TOPP_PSMFeatureExtractor and extra_features to the 32-entry list, on the first ProteinIdentification only

writeXLMSPeptideHit writes one Peptide per chain with the donor or acceptor cvParam, rebuilds the beta evidences from the BetaPepEv: lists, and emits the heavy half of a labelled pair by substituting the m/z, the retention time and the isoshifted calculated m/z into the light item's text

is_ppxl is true when a run declares is_cross_linking_experiment or SpectrumIdentificationProtocol == MS:1002494, which adds the XLMOD cv entry and groups all results of one spectrum reference into a single SpectrumIdentificationResult

evidence: Tier 3 source review. The expectations in tests/mzidentml.rs are transcribed from MzIdentMLFile_test.cpp and from the ten unmodified upstream fixtures: the 2/2/1/5 counts of msgf_mini, MS-GF+ 'Beta (v9979)', database.fasta, missed_cleavages 1000, the fixed modifications Carbamidomethyl (C) and Xlink:DTSSP[88] (Protein N-term), the 20 ppm parent tolerance, the protein accessions in their sorted order (sp|P0A9K9|SLYD_ECOLI before sp|P0A786|PYRB_ECOLI, which is the source's (score, accession) descending key), the four MS-GF:RawScore values 195/182/191/211 with their sequences and spectrum references, the 0.5 significance threshold and the pass_threshold pattern of spectrum 17 in whole.mzid, the Acetyl (N-term) variable modification, and the five modification-inference outcomes of issue #5443. No C++ mzIdentML reader or writer was built or executed and no differential output from those operations was retained, so nothing here is a tier 1 differential. Two expectations are independently derived rather than transcribed, and are marked as such in the test: the run date stays absent where the source substitutes DateTime::now(), and PeptideEvidence positions are converted from the file's 1-based values to OpenMS's documented 0-based ones, which the source does not do. The synthetic documents (duplicate ids, dangling peptide_ref and dBSequence_ref, an unreferenced SpectrumIdentificationList, two runs sharing one list, a prefixed namespace, a foreign namespace, non-ASCII accessions, an empty PeptideSequence, an out-of-range SubstitutionModification location, a negative rank, the C-terminal modification location, the ProteinDetectionList and every ReadOptions/WriteOptions ceiling) are tier 4, derived from mzIdentML1.3.0.xsd and from this port's own resource contract. The cross-linking expectations are transcribed the same way: the xl_pos1/xl_pos2 pairs, term specificities, sequence_beta values, xl_mod DSS, xl_mass 138.0680796, the heavy retention time 2125.5966796875 and m/z 725.109252929687841, the score -0.190406834856118 and the annotation strings [alpha|ci$b2], [beta|ci$y2] and [alpha|xi$b4] of sections 10 and 11, plus the counts of sections 12 to 15. The terminal-link, loop-link, empty-m/z and userParam-typing cases no upstream fixture reaches are tier 4, derived from the mzIdentML 1.3.0 schema and the crosslinking extension's cvParam definitions.
gaps: Cross-linking mzIdentML is read and written. What is still not ported is ANALYSIS/XLMS/OPXLHelper.h as a whole: only the six post-processing functions readMzIdentMLFile calls are reproduced, as private helpers of src/format/mzidentml.rs, and the search algorithm around them (enumerateCrossLinksAndMasses, digestDatabase, buildCandidates, buildPeptideIDs, combineTopRanksFromPairs, collectPrecursorCandidates, filterPrecursorsByTags, isoPeakMeans, computePrecursorError, buildFragmentAnnotations) keeps its own ledger entry. Reproducing the six locally duplicates logic that a later OPXLHelper port should own; the natural follow-up is to move them there and have this module call them.

MzIdentMLFile::isValid is not ported: it validates against the bundled XSD through XMLValidator, and the crate's only schema validator is behind the optional mzml-schema feature (libxml) and is mzML-specific. detectVersion, the half of isValid that selects the schema, is ported and tested.

MzIdentMLFile::isSemanticallyValid is not ported: it needs share/OpenMS/MAPPING/mzIdentML-mapping.xml, which is not among the crate's embedded resources, and FORMAT/VALIDATORS/MzIdentMLValidator.h, a separate unowned header.

MzIdentMLHandler's stream read path (onStartElement/onCharacters/onEndElement/handleCVParam_) is not ported. It is dead code upstream: MzIdentMLFile::load uses the DOM handler, and the items this path parses are accumulated into current_spectrum_id_, which nothing stores. The three public value types it fills (IdentificationHit, SpectrumIdentification, Identification) are ported as value types, because they are public API of the owned header.

The writer does not infer search modifications from the peptides when both modification lists are empty (MzIdentMLHandler.cpp:653 does, through ModificationDefinitionsSet::inferFromPeptides). Writing search parameters the input never declared would invent metadata, and the modifications are already in the Peptide elements.

A score type that maps to none of the writer's CV terms or aliases is written as the bare MS:1001143 term plus a userParam, exactly as the source does, and no reader recovers the number from that userParam. Such a score type therefore does not round-trip; the score types in the upstream fixtures (q-value, X\!Tandem:hyperscore, Mascot:score, MS-GF:RawScore) all do.

An identification run with no peptide identifications emits a SpectrumIdentification that references a SpectrumIdentificationList the document does not contain, because mzIdentML requires at least one SpectrumIdentificationResult per list. The source produces the same dangling reference. No fixture reaches it.

Enzyme site regular expressions are not written: mzIdentML has SiteRegexp, and the source omits it ('SiteRegex unstorable just now'), so SearchParameters::digestion_regex is lost on store. Run metadata other than spectra_data is lost as well, because the source's writeMetaInfos_ is applied to the search parameters only.
The source parallelises nothing in this family, so there is no OpenMP gap to record; the reader is a single pass over an in-memory tree and the writer a single pass over the document.

The ProteinIdentification::sort of src/identification.rs orders hits by score alone, while ProteinHit::ScoreMore/ScoreLess compare (score, accession); this reader applies the source's full key itself so a load reproduces the C++ order, but callers of that method still see the shorter key. Fixing it belongs to the package that owns src/identification.rs.
integration: The combined format wave registers this module in the reviewed API ledger, refreshes generated coverage and documentation floors, and wires its tests into the minimum-rust CI job.
external_reference_note: Isolated overload-resolution probe, compiled and run on kim with GCC13.3 C++20. Numeric global overload block copied from pinned StringUtils.h; appendToStr functions replaced by std::to_string adapters and Size by std::size_t. No full SDK include closure or linking; proves presence/selectability of numeric overloads in OpenMS namespace contexts and falsifies the claim only char overloads exist.
